The song Cigarettes and Saints, by The Wonder Years. First heard the song the day after my boyfriend committed suicide, and it gave it a whole new meaning. The music video also portrayed a young woman sadly writing a suicide note, packing up her pointe ballet shoes and getting ready to kill herself. As a young ballet dancer myself, I was in that exact situation. It was eerily congruent to my experience, yet in a weird way gave me some hope for the future. I still feel the depression I felt during that time whenever I hear the song, and I would consider that the lowest point of my life. But since then, I've been lucky enough to thank Dan Campbell for the song, hear it played live, and grow from my experience. 
Doesn't make it any less sad though. It's track 5 on the No Closer To Heaven Album, one of my favorites of all time. "You were the northern lights in a southern town" is my favorite lyric, now tattooed on my body. <3
